business_summary: Visa runs VisaNet, the world's largest electronic payments network. It does NOT lend money or issue cards; banks issue Visa-branded cards and Visa moves the authorization, clearing and settlement messages between the shopper's bank and the merchant's bank. It earns service fees on payments volume, data-processing fees per transaction, and high-margin international-transaction fees on cross-border payments, minus client incentives paid to banks. In the quarter ended 2026-06-30 it processed 71.7 billion transactions (+10%) and payments volume passed $4 trillion in a quarter for the first time. Revenue compounds with global consumer spending plus the long migration from cash and checks to digital payments, at ~60% operating margins and almost no incremental cost per transaction. Newer lanes - Visa Direct, value-added services, tokenization, B2B and a new stablecoin platform - extend the model beyond the traditional card swipe.

moat.type: Two-sided network effect (billions of cards x ~150m merchant locations) + global scale + brand/trust + high switching costs for issuers and acquirers; effective duopoly with Mastercard

quality.revenue_growth_3y: 10.9% CAGR (FY2022 $29.310B -> FY2025 $40.000B); accelerating - 9M FY2026 net revenue $33.764B vs $29.276B = +15.3% y/y
quality.gross_margin: n/a (network model, no COGS line). TTM GAAP operating margin 60.7% = $26.996B operating income / $44.488B net revenue, TTM to 2026-06-30
quality.roic: ~38% (TTM net income $22.592B / invested capital $59.036B = total equity $35.178B + total debt $23.858B at 2026-06-30); ~50% if invested capital is taken net of $13.792B cash and short-term investments
quality.net_debt_to_ebitda: ~0.35x (net debt $10.066B = total debt $23.858B minus cash $12.359B and short-term investments $1.433B, vs TTM operating income $26.996B plus ~$1.4B annualised D&A). Note: net debt rose from ~$2.4B at FY2025 year-end because 9M buybacks of $16.4B plus $3.9B dividends exceeded $16.3B operating cash flow.
quality.fcf_positive: yes - TTM FCF $21.013B ($22.580B operating cash flow minus $1.567B capex, TTM to 2026-06-30). Note TTM operating cash flow is slightly BELOW FY2025's $23.059B despite higher net income.

valuation.method: Average of two methods, assumptions held IDENTICAL to the 2026-Q2 thesis so the change comes only from fundamentals: (1) P/E - TTM GAAP diluted EPS $11.75 x 25/29/33 = $293.75/$340.75/$387.75; (2) FCF yield - TTM FCF per share $10.93 at 5.0/4.2/3.5% = $218.60/$260.24/$312.29. Computed by code/valuation.py. Margin of safety at $374.04 = -24.5% (expensive). Sensitivity: on TTM non-GAAP EPS $12.77 and tighter 4.5/3.8/3.2% yields the base rises to $328.98 (MoS -13.7%); the P/E leg alone on GAAP EPS gives a base of $340.75.

bull_case: Wide-moat duopoly: VisaNet's global web of issuers, acquirers and merchants cannot be rebuilt by a new entrant at any sensible cost; acceptance footprint and fraud/trust infrastructure are the barrier.
Growth is accelerating, not fading: 9M FY2026 net revenue $33.764B, +15.3% y/y, versus a 10.9% three-year CAGR through FY2025.

Record scale: Q3 FY2026 payments volume topped $4 trillion for the first time, processed transactions 71.7 billion (+10%), cross-border volume +13% constant-dollar - the highest-margin line is still the fastest growing.
Exceptional economics: 60.7% TTM GAAP operating margin, ~38% ROIC, capex of only $1.567B on $44.5B of TTM revenue, and $21.0B of TTM free cash flow.
Strong balance sheet and heavy capital return: $16.4B of buybacks and $3.9B of dividends in 9M FY2026, shrinking the share count; net-debt/EBITDA still only ~0.35x.

Optionality in new rails: Visa Stablecoin Platform launched July 2026, Visa Direct pre-funding with stablecoins, plus B2B and value-added services - Visa is positioning to carry the new rails rather than be bypassed by them.
Long secular tailwind: cash and checks remain a meaningful share of global payments, giving years of volume growth on top of nominal GDP.
risks: Valuation is the main risk today. At $374.04 the stock is ~24% ABOVE our base fair value of $300.49 and above the high end of the band ($350.02). It trades at 31.8x TTM GAAP EPS and a 2.96% FCF yield - there is no margin of safety, and a de-rating alone could cost 15-25% without anything going wrong operationally.

DOJ antitrust suit (filed September 2024) alleging illegal monopolisation of US debit network services is active, with major courtroom activity expected through 2026. An adverse outcome could force structural changes to Visa's debit business.

Merchant interchange litigation: the proposed US credit-interchange settlement was still awaiting court approval after an April 2026 preliminary-approval hearing; Visa took a further $237M litigation provision in Q3 FY2026 alone. Legal cost and headline risk are chronic, not one-off.

Cost growth is outrunning revenue: Q3 FY2026 GAAP operating expenses rose 19% versus 14% revenue growth, and GAAP net income grew only 7% while revenue grew 14%. A $563M severance charge and a 2,600-person (7% of workforce) layoff announced 2026-07-28 signal margin pressure and a business in transition.

Cash generation lagged profit: TTM operating cash flow of $22.580B is below FY2025's $23.059B even though TTM net income rose to $22.592B. Worth watching for a second quarter before concluding it is working capital / litigation escrow noise.

Disruption: account-to-account and real-time rails (FedNow, Pix, UPI-style systems), stablecoins and Big Tech wallets could route volume around the card networks over a decade. Visa's own stablecoin pivot is partly defensive.
Cyclicality: consumer spending and especially the high-margin cross-border travel line fall in recessions.
Regulatory fee caps: interchange or network-fee regulation in the US or EU remains a perennial threat to the economics.
what_would_break_thesis: GAAP operating margin falls below 50% for two consecutive fiscal quarters (TTM base today is 60.7%) - erosion of network pricing power.
Net revenue shrinks year-over-year for two consecutive quarters outside a clearly identified macro recession - signals structural volume loss to alternative rails.
Processed-transaction growth falls below 3% year-over-year for two consecutive quarters while global card spending is still growing - evidence of share loss.
Cross-border volume growth (constant-dollar) turns negative for two consecutive quarters outside a travel shock - permanent loss of the highest-margin business.
Net-debt-to-EBITDA rises above 2.0x (currently ~0.35x) - balance-sheet deterioration or value-destroying M&A.
Free cash flow turns negative for a full fiscal year, or TTM free cash flow falls below 60% of TTM net income for two consecutive quarters.
A final, non-appealable regulatory ruling or settlement that structurally caps interchange or network fees in the US or EU and is expected to cut net revenue by more than ~15%.
An adverse final judgment in the DOJ debit antitrust case that forces divestiture or mandated unbundling of Visa's US debit business.
GAAP operating expenses grow faster than net revenue for four consecutive quarters (currently 19% vs 14% in Q3 FY2026) - a persistent, not transitional, cost problem.
A serious accounting red flag or restatement.
catalysts: Q4 and full-year FY2026 earnings, expected late October 2026 - watch cross-border volume, client incentives, and whether opex growth re-converges with revenue growth.
Court decision on preliminary/final approval of the US merchant credit-interchange settlement.
Rulings and trial milestones in the DOJ US debit antitrust case through 2026.
Evidence that the Visa Stablecoin Platform and Visa Direct stablecoin pre-funding are winning volume rather than cannibalising it.
Continued share-count reduction from the buyback programme.
A market de-rating or a consumer-spending scare that brings the price toward the $300-$350 fair-value band - the entry we are waiting for.
